name: TMAG5273 3D Hall-effect sensor
description: Texas Instruments low-power linear 3D Hall-effect sensor: X, Y and Z magnetic field (A1: ±40 or ±80 mT, 16-bit results) plus an on-chip temperature sensor, read over I2C. Chip runs on 1.7–3.6 V; the breakout adds a 3.3 V regulator and I2C level shifting. Sold as: Adafruit TMAG5273 3D Hall Effect Magnetometer Breakout, A1 variant (±40/±80 mT; 6-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, INT; plus two STEMMA QT), I2C address 0x35.
eli5: Feels a nearby magnet and tells your board how strong its pull is in three directions, great for magnetic knobs and joysticks.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply input to the on-board 3.3 V regulator, 3–5 V; use the same voltage as your board's logic

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the board, 3–5 V logic)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the board, 3–5 V logic)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output / conversion trigger input (open-drain, 3.3 V side); not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: Adafruit TMAG5273 A1 3D Hall Effect Magnetometer Breakout STEMMA QT
buildNotes: Check the chip first: MANUFACTURER_ID (0x0E/0x0F) reads 0x49, 0x54 ("TI"); DEVICE_ID (0x0D) bits 1-0 = 1 for A1 (±40/±80 mT), 2 for A2 (±133/±266 mT).

Set up: DEVICE_CONFIG_1 (0x00) = 0x14 (32x averaging), SENSOR_CONFIG_1 (0x02) = 0x70 (X, Y, Z on), T_CONFIG (0x07) = 0x01 (temperature on), then DEVICE_CONFIG_2 (0x01) = 0x12 (low-noise, continuous measure).
Read 8 bytes from 0x10: T, X, Y, Z, each 16-bit two's complement MSB first. Bit 7 of the register address byte is a conversion trigger, so keep it 0 for plain reads.
Field: B = raw × 2 × range / 65536 mT (A1 default ±40 mT: 1.2207 µT per LSB). Temperature: T = 25 + (raw − 17508) / 58 °C.
Meant for magnets close by (rotary knobs, joysticks, lid sensors), not the Earth's field. Steel screws and the breadboard's metal clips shift the zero reading.
The A2 board looks identical but has ±133/±266 mT ranges; the driver reads DEVICE_ID and scales automatically.

driver.code:
# TMAG5273 3D linear Hall-effect sensor (Texas Instruments), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the TI TMAG5273 datasheet (SLYS045C):
#  - registers: DEVICE_CONFIG_1 0x00, DEVICE_CONFIG_2 0x01, SENSOR_CONFIG_1 0x02,
#    SENSOR_CONFIG_2 0x03, T_CONFIG 0x07, DEVICE_ID 0x0D, MANUFACTURER_ID 0x0E/0x0F ("TI" = 0x5449),
#    T/X/Y/Z results 0x10..0x17 (16-bit two's complement, MSB first), CONV_STATUS 0x18
#  - standard 3-byte I2C read: the register byte's bit 7 is the conversion trigger, so it is kept 0 here
#  - B = raw / 2^16 * 2 * BR (Equation 10), BR = 40/80 mT (A1) or 133/266 mT (A2)
#  - T = 25 + (raw - 17508) / 58 degC (Equation 12, TSENS_T0, TADC_T0, TADC_RES)
import time

_DEVICE_CONFIG_1 = 0x00
_DEVICE_CONFIG_2 = 0x01
_SENSOR_CONFIG_1 = 0x02
_SENSOR_CONFIG_2 = 0x03
_T_CONFIG = 0x07
_DEVICE_ID = 0x0D
_MANUFACTURER_ID_LSB = 0x0E
_T_MSB_RESULT = 0x10
_CONV_STATUS = 0x18

_TADC_T0 = 17508
_TADC_RES = 58.0
_TSENS_T0 = 25.0


def _s16(hi, lo):
    v = (hi << 8) | lo
    return v - 0x10000 if v & 0x8000 else v


class TMAG5273:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x35, wide_range=False, avg=5):
        """addr: 0x35 for TMAG5273A1/A2 (Adafruit board default).
        wide_range: False = +-40 mT (A1) / +-133 mT (A2); True = +-80 mT / +-266 mT.
        avg: CONV_AVG 0..5 (1x..32x averaging)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # tstart_power_up 270 us
        mid = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(addr, _MANUFACTURER_ID_LSB, 2)
        if mid[0] != 0x49 or mid[1] != 0x54:
            raise OSError('TMAG5273 not found (manufacturer ID 0x%02X%02X)' % (mid[1], mid[0]))
        ver = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(addr, _DEVICE_ID, 1)[0] & 0x03
        if ver == 1:
            base = 40.0
        elif ver == 2:
            base = 133.0
        else:
            raise OSError('TMAG5273 unknown DEVICE_ID version %d' % ver)
        self.range_mt = base * (2 if wide_range else 1)
        # CRC off, no magnet tempco, CONV_AVG, standard 3-byte I2C read
        self._w(_DEVICE_CONFIG_1, (avg & 0x07) << 2)
        # MAG_CH_EN = 7h (X, Y, Z), SLEEPTIME unused
        self._w(_SENSOR_CONFIG_1, 0x70)
        # no angle calc; X_Y_RANGE and Z_RANGE
        r = 0x03 if wide_range else 0x00
        self._w(_SENSOR_CONFIG_2, r)
        # temperature channel on, no threshold
        self._w(_T_CONFIG, 0x01)
        # low-noise mode, glitch filter on, I2C trigger, continuous measure mode
        self._w(_DEVICE_CONFIG_2, 0x12)
        # tstart_measure 70 us + up to 4 channels x 32 samples (about 3.3 ms)
        time.sleep_ms(5)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes((val,)))

    def read(self):
        """Return (x, y, z) in mT and the chip temperature in degC."""
        for _ in range(50):
            if self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _CONV_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x01:
                break
            time.sleep_ms(1)
        else:
            raise OSError('TMAG5273: no conversion result')
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _T_MSB_RESULT, 8)
        t_raw = _s16(d[0], d[1])
        k = 2 * self.range_mt / 65536
        x = _s16(d[2], d[3]) * k
        y = _s16(d[4], d[5]) * k
        z = _s16(d[6], d[7]) * k
        temp = _TSENS_T0 + (t_raw - _TADC_T0) / _TADC_RES
        return x, y, z, temp

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from tmag5273 import TMAG5273

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
mag = TMAG5273(i2c)
while True:
    x, y, z, t = mag.read()
    print('X=%.2f Y=%.2f Z=%.2f mT T=%.1fC' % (x, y, z, t))
    time.sleep(1)
